definition: Next Sentence Prediction — BERT’s auxiliary pretraining task of predicting whether one sentence follows another; later dropped in models like RoBERTa as unnecessary.
details: Next Sentence Prediction — BERT’s auxiliary pretraining task of predicting whether one sentence follows another; later dropped in models like RoBERTa as unnecessary.

explainer.lead: NSP was an auxiliary pretraining task in BERT that taught the model to judge whether one sentence follows another. It shaped early language-model pretraining but was later shown to be droppable.

tiers.eli5: Show a model two sentences and ask: does the second one come right after the first? Practising that teaches it how text hangs together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers included NSP alongside masked-language-model loss when pretraining BERT-style encoders; the pitfall is that the task is easy and noisy, so it can add cost without helping downstream accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: Given sentence pair (A, B), the model predicts a binary label: IsNext if B truly follows A in the source text, NotNext if B is a random replacement. BERT reported that removing NSP hurts some tasks, but RoBERTa showed the task is unnecessary when pretraining is otherwise improved.

explainer.example: From a document, pair a real adjacent sentence as IsNext and swap in a sentence from another document as NotNext; the model learns to score the pair.
